svg.text: B-A FALLTURM — the vertical food tower
Food falls from the box through floorless stages (wash/peel, cut) into the vessel; the wash water later takes exactly the same path.
wash ≈ 15 L, 0.7 kWh, then 70 °C air 15 min
nothing stores food: a disc under a sleeve, a cutter over a grid
Stages swing out of the shaft
top view: arms on the rear post, 90°
rice, flour, liquids: free fall through the open shaft —
the Ø 100 stream never touches the 180 mm wall
The wash takes the food's path
a wash cartridge docks where the box was
150 m³/h, 15 min, from the top fan
whatever the food could reach, the water reaches too
(weak: flat items need a separate flat station)
1/8 The tipper dock turns the box over (open lid, pulse-tilt, stops on weight); the potatoes fall through the shutter.
2/8 L4: the abrasive disc spins under the sleeve with water; the peel leaves as slurry through the gap and goes to waste.
3/8 The sleeve lifts: the peeled potatoes are thrown off the disc and fall through the funnel; the diverter now points to the shaft.
4/8 L3: the slicing disc over the 10 mm grid dices them; the cubes fall into the vessel raised on the Z-lift.
5/8 The vessel goes down onto the induction hob; the tool head swings in from the side to stir.
6/8 Rice: both stages swing out of the shaft and the rice falls freely from its own lid into the raised vessel.
7/8 Wash: a wash cartridge docks where the box was; the jets, the ring nozzles and the spinning discs follow the food path.
8/8 Then 70 °C air from the top fan dries the whole tower; peel and solids are caught by the screen below.
